newsitem.title: UK: Brent sees clocking but paper market strong.
newsitem.headline: Brent sees clocking but paper market strong.

text.p: The Brent paper market gained substantial ground over the day as traders came out to cover short positions but buying interest in physical benchmark Brent crude was limited.
Of the two Brent (July 17-19) cargoes in Wednesday's paper chains, the Shell system yet again kept one but, somewhat surprisingly, British Petroleum was clocked with the other.
"People don't really want to have the physical oil but won't sell their paper positions, so the value of paper continues to rise," one trader said.
August Brent on the IPE was down just three cents by 1700 GMT at $18.77 a barrel. The prompt July/August paper spread was bid up to 15 cents with the best offer at +20 cents.
The spread traded earlier at +15 cents.
Further out the market was steadier with Aug/Sep at -7/-5 cents and Sep/Oct valued around deals at -7 and -8 cents.

The only Brent cargo from the first half of the July loading programme expected by many to be reoffered on the market was one of Wednesday's dates. The value of dated Brent held steady between August Brent -5 cents and evens.

No physical deals were reported though levels were expected to hold steady. The only possible exception being Ekofisk where some prompt Ekofisk was heard offered as a result of the delay in the return of the Wilhelmshaven refinery.
The 185,000 bpd refinery was expected to return earlier this week after a full months maintenance. Traders said the return was being delayed but they did not know for how long.

CFDs gained ground with next week's (7-11) dates trading earlier at August -5 cents but bid in late talk up to August evens. Further out less interest was heard and the July 14-18 dates talked around Aug -15/-12 cents.
Mediterranean crude markets were quiet but firm, continuing to draw support from uncertainty over the timing of a resumption of Iraqi exports.
But the strength in benchmark Russian Urals was beginning to hurt refiners, with some considering cutting back crude runs.
"Margins are not very good in this area," said a trader.
"It's not clear what is going to be available (from Iraq) in July so people prefer not to take any action until more information is available," he said.
